summary.para: The MBNCSUtil namespace provides 100%-managed types for the implementation of Battle.net logon authorization.
This code should run on any x86-based system with the Common-Language Infrastructure. No native Windows calls are used. Big-endian systems are not supported.

This code is based upon Eric Naseth's (shadypalm88's) BNCSUtil 1.0.4, as well as Ron Bowes' (iago's) various Java implementations. However, most code is original C#, unless otherwise noted, by Robert Paveza (MyndFyre).

summary.para: As of version 1.2.0.4, MBNCSUtil is licensed under a modified version of the BSD License. Please see the details in the accompanying LICENSE.TXT for specific terms.

The major, minor, and build numbers of the assembly match those of the BNCSUtil version they are based on. The first version of this code was based on version 1.0.4 of BNCSUtil, and so the first version of MBNCSUtil was 1.0.4.0.

Add mbncsutil.dll to your project as a reference (in Visual Studio .NET, right-click on your project, choose "Add Reference...", and under the .NET tab, select "Browse...". Locate the assembly, and select it to add it to your project).

The language-neutral version of this project depends on the English-language resources (culture "en") so during deployment, at the very least the /en/ subfolder must be present. Additional languages may be deployed in the subfolder and may be accessed by setting regional options in the standard way or otherwise.
If you are recreating the project from the source code and not using the provided Visual C# 2003 projects, then the following precompilation constants will be important:
summary.list:
Symbol Meaning
DEBUG;UNSAFE;NET_1_1_OR_NEWER
DEBUG Debugging helpers including NextXxx properties on the reader classes are included, as well as certain text outputs to tracing listeners for debugging aid.
UNSAFE
As of build 1.3.0.6, this symbol is no longer required. It may be defined to produce code that may be more efficient but is unverifiable (it uses pointers); if it is undefined, the code will be 100% verifiable but may be less efficient (it creates streams).
As of build 1.0.4.0, this symbol is required for any and all X-SHA-1 hashing to function properly in MBNCSUtil (this includes the OldAuth class and CdKey class). Work is being done to remove unsafe code from MBNCSUtil, but it is not a priority.
NET_1_1_OR_NEWER A problem was found in version 1.2.0.4 (and presumably earlier versions) that caused MBNCSUtil to fail when running the revision check due to a new method added in .NET 1.1 that was not available in .NET 1.0. This only affected users working in the 1.0 environment. Rebuilds in .NET 2.0 are asked to follow this pattern and mark code that is for 2.0 only or newer with the symbol NET_2_0_OR_NEWER, but this will not be standardized until MBNCSUtil is released for .NET 2.0.

item.description: IMPORTANT - corrected errors in the DataReader and BncsReader classes that caused exceptions to be raised when using them with a Stream. The constructors for these classes have changed where they accept a Stream parameter, so code may need to be changed to accomodate this fix. The COM interfaces have been changed as well. (Thanks to BaDDBlooD for finding and reporting this issue).
IMPORTANT - fixed an issue when using the NLS class to calculate the logon proof when not creating an account. (Thanks to cheeseybulb01 for finding and reporting this issue).
NEW FEATURE - added the DataFormatter static class for convenient binary data output.

Changed the IDataReader and IBncsReader interfaces on the relevant classes so that the InitializeXxx() methods and Initialized property are explicitly implemented. This was also done in the NLS and CdKey classes.

Added support for not using pointers to the CdKey and XSha1 classes; the project may now be built without defining the UNSAFE constant. In Visual Studio 2002 or 2003, select the Debug .NET 1.0 Safe, Debug .NET 1.1 Safe, Release .NET 1.0 Safe, or Release .NET 1.1 Safe solution configuration to build the library without unsafe code. To continue to build with unsafe code, which may be more efficient, build using the Debug .NET 1.0, Debug .NET 1.1, Release .NET 1.0, or Release .NET 1.1 configurations, depending on which version of the .NET runtime you are using.

Some code, particularly in the BncsReader and DataReader classes, may be somewhat obscure and confusing (these have been denoted as "hacked" sections). C# does not allow for certain expressions to be used, and in order to accomodate the new (Stream, int) base constructor and explicit interface implementations, some funny code additions had to be made. These are not externally visible to linked code, but if you browse the source, you will notice them. They can be ignored.
VERY IMPORTANT - corrected an error in the new BncsReader class that prevented new packet creation following the first call to the BncsReader constructor on the same NetworkStream.

Changed the IDataBuffer interface to use named functions for InsertXxx instead of overloads, which were not COM-compliant. This change was made to the DataBuffer class as well, although the Insert methods were preserved.
Corrected inconsistency that was still preventing the use of satellite assemblies to get appropriate localized error strings.

Made the application of ObsoleteAttribute to COM-only accessors more consistent. Constructors, methods, and classes that are only intended to be used through COM are now marked as such and will generate a compilation error if you attempt to use them through .NET.
Added examples to several classes' documentation.

VERY IMPORTANT - corrected an error in the MBNCSUtil localization framework that caused exceptions to be invalid (when an exception was thrown, it was dependent on localized strings, and the localization framework was not properly referencing the satellite assemblies. MBNCSUtil worked correctly as long as you did not cause any exceptions, but debugging your code would have been next to impossible had you introduced exceptions.

Added packet buffer classes DataBuffer and BncsPacket. The DataBuffer class is a generalized packet buffer and can have some of its methods overridden to provide specialized protocol support. An example of this is the BncsPacket class, which overrides the GetData method to insert the BNCS header. These classes should be considered beta-quality code until you have tested them. They have not been tested extensively in MBNCSUtil, although they have been used in other software packages.

Added data reader classes (commonly called packet "debuffer" classes) DataReader and BncsReader. These classes parallel the DataBuffer and BncsPacket classes in function, but operate in the other direction (they are for reading data instead of writing it). These classes should be considered beta-quality code until you have tested them. They have not been tested extensively in MBNCSUtil, although they have been used in other software packages.

Changed licensing scheme from GNU GPL to a modified version of the FreeBSD license. I believe that to have truly "free" software you must not restrict the rights of the user so that only "free" software can come from it.
Added Spanish (es) localization resource file. Please forward comments.
Code and ResX files are now available on the web:

Applied COM attributes and created interfaces to enable COM-aware access. All COM interfaces are contained within the MBNCSUtil.Com namespace, and for classes that are static-accessor-only, wrapper classes were created also within the MBNCSUtil.Com namespace. The NLS and CdKey classes were updated for interoperability with COM as well.

Added language support: removed English-language Exception messages (although not parameter name strings for argument-related exceptions) and put them into MBNCSUtil.en.resx. MBNCSUtil.en.resx could be converted into other languages for other cultures, and the result project recompiled.

Fixed a problem related to CD key decoding that would prevent this library from running on SSCLI Linux-based systems. Specifically, an integer rotation function ROL was implemented in managed code rather than by calling the MS VC runtime _lrotl function through P/Invoke.
Changed the NLS and CdKey classes to instance classes rather than context-based static classes.
Fixed several bugs relating to X-SHA-1 as well as CD key decoding.
